reference_sql:
SELECT promo_id, product_id,
       COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY promo_id) AS promo_products
FROM promotion_products
alternatives:
WITH promo_counts AS (  -- one row per promotion with products
  SELECT promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY promo_id
)
SELECT pp.promo_id, pp.product_id, pc.n_products AS promo_products
FROM promotion_products pp
JOIN promo_counts pc ON pc.promo_id = pp.promo_id

SELECT pp.promo_id, pp.product_id,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM promotion_products pp2 WHERE pp2.promo_id = pp.promo_id) AS promo_products
FROM promotion_products pp

other_way.sql:
WITH promo_counts AS (  -- one row per promotion with products
  SELECT promo_id, COUNT(*) AS n_products
  FROM promotion_products
  GROUP BY promo_id
)
SELECT pp.promo_id, pp.product_id, pc.n_products AS promo_products
FROM promotion_products pp
JOIN promo_counts pc ON pc.promo_id = pp.promo_id
other_way.tradeoff: A per-promotion count joined back is portable, but it reads the bridge table twice.
